verdict.rationale: Fly.io's own materials directly cover this story: Sprites and Machines are described as hardware-isolated VMs, explicitly pitched for running untrusted code, with a clean baseline per request, egress locking, and disposability. Machines can also be created and destroyed directly via the API. missing for 10: in-depth technical documentation of the isolation mechanism and sandbox lifecycle (the evidence is mostly homepage marketing copy), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the sandboxing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run untrusted code in hardware-isolated, disposable sandboxes

citations.quote: Run it in a hardware-isolated VM. A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state. Egress-locked and disposable.
Run untrusted code, evals, and RL rollouts in parallel. Checkpoint what works, throw away the rest.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second
You can create and destroy Machines directly, and you have control over every Machine’s lifecycle, resources, and region placement.
